spaces.name: domain
spaces.label: **Domain**
spaces.rule: The product's own model. Never serialized directly; never a database row; never a view model.

spaces.name: wire
spaces.label: **Wire**
spaces.rule: Contract DTOs and identifiers. Never a domain entity; never persisted as-is as the canonical store.

spaces.name: UI
spaces.label: **UI**
spaces.rule: View state and presentation. Never a transport DTO; never a domain object.

spaces.name: storage
spaces.label: **Storage**
spaces.rule: Database schema, native file format, cache format. Distinct from both Domain and Wire.

spaces.name: commercial
spaces.label: **Commercial**
spaces.rule: Plan, Offer, Price, Entitlement, Credit, Ledger. Never a Feature Flag; never a Permission.

terms.definition: An independent deployment of ArcForges Cloud that is its own authority: the Official realm, or a self-hosted realm. Objects are never identical across realms even when the account email matches. Every cross-device and cross-application reference is realm-aware.
A cloud account identity within a realm.
A signed-out native operator without a Cloud UserId. May use product-specific native functions; has no official AI access or account-free notebook service.
A single-user Cloud data, device, sync, billing and permission boundary. One owner in a realm; never a team/member container or panel layout.
A desktop panel/window arrangement. The mandatory term for what some products elsewhere call a "workspace".
Excluded by [P2-006](../decisions/phase-2-specification-decisions.md#rule-p2-006): no organization, team, membership, invitation or collaboration-specific schema reservation.
A registered client machine or handset within a realm.
One installed copy of one product on one device. Long-lived.
One running process of one product. Per-launch.
The stable product identity: `arcnotes`, `arcscope`, `arcslate`, `companion`. Never a process id, never a product-scope, never a licence unit.
An OS window belonging to an Instance. An Instance may own several.
An authenticated interaction lifetime. Distinct from Connection, from Device and from Subscription.
A transport-level link (Named Pipe/UDS stream, HTTP connection, realtime connection). Carries no identity of its own.
Who a principal is.
On whose authority an operation runs.
What actually performs an operation.
Which process issued a call. Never a substitute for Actor.
A security subject that may hold permissions: a human User, or a scoped delegate.
An agent acting on behalf of a user session. Never an independent superuser identity, never a security principal in its own right.
The operating-system account that owns local IPC endpoints and secure storage.
A durable business object owned by exactly one product in exactly one realm.

A stable, realm-aware, typed reference to a Resource: identity plus metadata. Never resource content, never a file path, never a capability token, never a permission token, never a universal domain entity, never a selection.
The stable identifier inside a ResourceRef. Never reused.
The namespaced type of a Resource, e.g. `arcnotes.document`, `arcscope.session`, `arcslate.project`.
A path, URI or device address by which external content is reached. Never a Resource Identity.
Content whose bytes ArcForges owns and garbage-collects.
Content that remains under the user's own control, referenced but not owned.
A meaningful work result produced by a Task, Agent or App — a document, report, session, rendered video, project or ordinary file. Never "an ArcChat file".
A reference to an Artifact, carrying provenance and task relationship. Distinct from `ResourceRef`. Never a permission token.
A rendered or summarised view of an Artifact. Never the Artifact's authority.
A user-directed navigation address into a product surface. Never a command. Never a permission token.
The recorded origin of a derived object: source resource, task, actor, revision.

A semantic, versioned, strongly typed operation a product exposes to the platform. Identified by a `capabilityId` string used only for discovery, display, policy, tool selection, routing and audit — never as the call mechanism.

The declared metadata of a Capability: identity, provider app/instance, typed method identity, contract version and feature flags, input/output summary, whether it writes state, required scope, risk level, whether confirmation is mandatory, dry-run/undo/cancel support, resource size, expected duration and concurrency limits.
A user- or agent-visible intent that may be fulfilled by one or more Capability invocations. Not itself a Capability.
A menu item, button or shortcut. Never a Capability.
One call of one Capability. Distinct from `CommandId`, and distinct from a Task Step.
The idempotency key of a write command. Distinct from `InvocationId` and from `AttemptId`.
What the caller is currently working on. References Resources; is not itself a Resource.
A product-side component that answers "what is the user looking at / has selected". Not a search engine, not a resource database.
A bounded, frozen set of context handed to a run. Never an entire knowledge source, never a copy of all data.
Volatile UI state. Never a durable resource identity.
A short-lived, narrowly scoped credential authorising one controlled access. Distinct from `ResourceRef`.
The meaning and obligations of a Capability.
The serialized shape by which a Capability is called. Distinct from the Semantic Contract.
What the user asked for, before any plan exists.
Durable Cloud agent work with a lifecycle and persistent record. Ordinary render, capture, import or simulation jobs are not agent Tasks.
One execution of a Task. A Task may have several Runs.
One planned unit inside a Run.
One execution try of a Step. Distinct from `CommandId`.
The Cloud agent module holding authoritative Task/Run/Step/Attempt state. A desktop tool owner is not a Task Owner.
The single Cloud harness sequencing agent work and authorized tools. Each application's assistant presents its tasks and bridges only its own local tools; it does not run another orchestrator.
Cloud for the AI runtime. Desktop/Cloud/Hybrid labels on a task describe tool locality only; they never select another model loop.
A stable Cloud Agent Task reference for query/correlation, never an RPC connection or product job identity.
An authoritative point-in-time projection of Task state, retrievable over HTTP.
A best-effort realtime notification. Never task authority.
A resumable execution marker inside a Run. Never an Undo entry; never a Recovery Journal.
A forward action that reverses the observable effect of a completed step. Never a transaction rollback.
A bounded, parameter-bound, time-limited human authorisation of a specific pending operation. Never a persistent permission grant, never step-up authentication, never steering.
A user's execution-direction update to an active Task. Never an approval, never an ordinary conversation message.
A derived presentation flag over one or more pending Approvals or errors. Never a Task state.
A per-task or per-automation ceiling on cost, credits, time or steps. Never an Entitlement.
A durable definition that creates Tasks when a Trigger fires. Never itself a Task.
One firing of an Automation. Never a Task retry.
The configured rule.
One event matching the rule.
The recorded sequence of steps, invocations, decisions and results for a Run, safe to show. Never model chain-of-thought; never an Audit record.
Bounded non-agent work owned by a product or Cloud module: capture, render, import, indexing, simulation. It has its own progress/cancel/recovery contract, never a second model loop.
Typed, owner-qualified reference to a product job that a Cloud Task may observe through tools. Not a TaskHandle.
Normalized actual provider usage per attempt/category, with provenance and settled/unknown status; not a prompt-size estimate.
Actual billable provider units multiplied by the applicable supplier-rate snapshot, independently reconciled against provider charges.
Versioned rates converting eligible usage to customer service units; distinct from supplier cost and payment price.
A bounded recoverable service-unit balance replenishing during eligible service time. Not a monthly cash or purchased-credit lot.
Separate purchased/compensation lots consumed only with explicit consent and an eligible service term. Credit ownership alone grants no official AI access.
One validated, immutable version/hash of operator deployment configuration, archived for audit; not a mutable rewrite of historical usage or paid grants.
An ordered thread of Messages. Not a Task.
One turn in a Conversation. Not a Tool Call.
An ArcChat-scoped grouping of conversations, context references and settings. **Not** a Workspace, **not** an `ArcScope.Project`, **not** an `ArcSlate.Project`.
A saved configuration of model, tools, instructions and limits. Not a running agent; not a model; not a security principal.
Reusable guidance and configuration that shapes agent behaviour. Not a Capability; not extension code; not MCP; not a permission grant.
ArcChat-owned durable user-preference recall. Not ArcNotes knowledge; not a conversation summary.
The local platform coordination plane hosted inside the owning professional application process.
An `ArtifactRef` held by ArcChat. Never the underlying owned object.
The top-level ArcNotes container. **Not** a Workspace.
A hierarchical container. **Not** a Tag.
The canonical document object. **Not** a file; **not** a Markdown file.
The addressable unit inside a Document, with a stable `BlockId`. **Not** a Markdown line.
Typed metadata on a Document or Block. **Not** document content.
A non-hierarchical label.
A stored query and presentation over typed properties. Confers **no ownership** of the objects it lists.
A referenced binary managed by ArcNotes. Never base64 embedded in canonical content.
Retired by [P2-006](../decisions/phase-2-specification-decisions.md#rule-p2-006). Edgeless, whiteboard, shape/connector/frame workspaces are excluded.
Bounded note organization through scalar properties, queries and table/list Saved Views; not the SQLite/D1 storage schema or a formula/relation/rollup platform.
Retired by [P2-006](../decisions/phase-2-specification-decisions.md#rule-p2-006). Presentations, slide generation, frame ordering and presentation navigation are excluded.
A document-local task item. **Not** an ArcChat Agent Task.
An ArcScope-scoped container of sources, sessions and analyses. **Not** an ArcForges Workspace.
Physical or logical hardware. **Not** a DataSource.
A configured source definition.
Stored connection settings. **Not** a live Connection.
An observation lifetime. **Not** a Connection; **not** a Capture.
A recorded data acquisition within a Session.
A transport-level stream of values. **Not** a Signal.
A semantically typed, named quantity. **Not** an Event.
A discrete occurrence in time.
Acquired versus computed. Never conflated.
A quantified reading with units and uncertainty. **Not** an Analysis.
An interpretation over measurements.
A protocol interpreter producing Decoder Output. **Decoder Output ≠ Raw Data.**
A non-destructive marking. **Never** a data mutation.
A side-by-side relation between sessions or captures. **Not** a merge.
An ArcScope-owned report artifact. **Not** an ArcNotes Document.
Display state. Pausing the view never pauses the capture.
Persisted capture data, distinct from LiveView display state.
Downsampling for rendering only. Never the measurement data.
A Cloud-owned simulator definition.
An immutable scenario version.
A non-agent simulator product job.
An immutable segment of a simulation result.
An ordered event in a simulation run.
The editing project. **Not** a Sequence; **not** a media folder.
A timeline composition. **Not** a Timeline Clip.
The temporal arrangement inside a Sequence.
A lane within a Timeline.
A placed reference to source media with in/out points. **Not** the source media.
The managed identity of a piece of media. **Not** a file path; **not** a Clip.
Source-relative versus composition-relative time. Never interchangeable.
Distinct rate domains. Never the same clock.
A declared relation between adjacent clips. **Not** an incidental overlap.
Type versus applied instance with parameters.
A time-anchored parameter value. **Not** the current parameter value.
A lower-cost stand-in for original media. **Not** the original; **not** a render cache.
Rebuildable rendered output. **Never** project authority.
An ArcSlate-owned native product render/export Job, distinct from a Cloud Agent Task and UI progress dialog.
The produced media file. **Not** the ArcSlate Project.
Machine text versus authored, timed, styled display text.

ArcSlate retains product direction only, not a model, identity or automatic migration.
